harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created an SSH CA on node1 (/etc/ssh/ca/ssh_ca), signed the ed25519 host key into /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub with principals node1/NODE_IP/localhost, configured sshd via HostCertificate, and verified a client trusting only an @cert-authority line (no pinned host key) connects successfully while a client with no CA trust is rejected. Completed mandatory single-node restart evidence protocol: captured boot_id baseline, rebooted via `shutdown -r now`, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed, and re-verified sshd active plus CA-trusted SSH connection worked post-reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected OS/sshd version (RHEL7.9, OpenSSH 7.4p1) and confirmed sudo access
Generated ed25519 SSH CA keypair at /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_ca(.pub) owned root:root, 600/644 perms
Signed /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub as a host certificate (10yr validity, principals node1,NODE_IP,node1,localhost) producing /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub
Added 'HostCertificate /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub' to /etc/ssh/sshd_config, validated with sshd -t, reloaded sshd
Verified: client with only '@cert-authority node1,NODE_IP <ca-pub>' in known_hosts (no pinned host key) connects and authenticates successfully via cluster SSH key
Falsification check: client with empty known_hosts and StrictHostKeyChecking=yes is rejected, proving the CA trust (not laxness) enables the connection
Captured pre-restart boot_id baseline and service/file health
Rebooted node1 via 'shutdown -r now', polled until SSH/exec available again
Confirmed boot_id changed post-reboot (real restart, not just service restart)
Re-verified sshd active, CA and cert files persisted, and CA-trusted SSH connection succeeds post-reboot

evidence.requirement: SSH CA created on node1
evidence.summary: ssh-keygen generated /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_ca and ssh_ca.pub, root-owned with correct permissions

evidence.requirement: Host key signed by the CA into a certificate
evidence.summary: ssh-keygen -s produced ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub; ssh-keygen -L confirms Signing CA matches the created CA, principals include node1 and NODE_IP

evidence.requirement: sshd configured to present the certificate
evidence.summary: HostCertificate directive added, sshd -t passed, sshd reloaded successfully

evidence.requirement: Client trusting only the CA (no host-key pinning) connects successfully
evidence.summary: ssh with UserKnownHostsFile containing only '@cert-authority' CA line (no pinned host key) and StrictHostKeyChecking=yes succeeded, printing CERT_TRUSTED_CONNECT_OK

evidence.requirement: Falsification: CA trust is what enables the connection
evidence.summary: Same client config but empty known_hosts (no CA trust) is rejected with 'Host key verification failed'

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline (boot identity, sshd, cert/CA files)
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id d72bd4ec..., sshd active, cert and CA files present before reboot

evidence.requirement: Restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: shutdown -r now issued in background with nohup; connection closed by remote host confirming the reboot command was accepted and executing

evidence.requirement: Node polled until command execution available again
evidence.summary: Two timed-out polls during reboot, then a successful poll once node1 came back up

evidence.requirement: Proof of changed boot identity (real restart, not just uptime/service evidence)
evidence.summary: boot_id changed from d72bd4ec-4e55-42df-9c71-99b4f4ace0ec to e127ee7d-02a1-42b3-8d52-753a43dfb747, and uptime -s shows a fresh boot time

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required services/data (CA-cert SSH trust)
evidence.summary: sshd active and CA/cert files present after reboot; CA-trusted client connection re-verified successfully post-reboot

Completed mandatory single-node restart evidence protocol: captured boot_id baseline, rebooted via `shutdown -r now`, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed, and re-verified sshd active plus CA-trusted SSH connection worked post-reboot.
